description: Mina, a bicycle mechanic, must decide whether to accept Cal's proposed barter of bicycle work for home-cooked dinners. Mina's housemate Ruth is present because the dinners would be brought into their shared home.

shared_context.S1: Mina has offered to tune one neighbor's bicycle in exchange for goods or services rather than cash.
shared_context.S2: Cal has said he is interested in making a barter arrangement for his bicycle.
shared_context.S3: The arrangement will be discussed and agreed verbally at Mina and Ruth's kitchen table.
shared_context.S4: Their kitchen-table routine requires the person making an offer to enter the complete offer in the formal disclosure field first, rather than merely discussing it; Cal goes first, Ruth enters household requirements second, and Mina then reads every agreed field back for confirmation before making the final call.
shared_context.S5: Mina writes the disclosed terms and household requirements down using labeled fields for arrangement, tune-up scope, dinner count, servings, delivery schedule, cash component, and food safety.

PF1.text: Cal's complete offer is one bicycle tune-up covering the drivetrain, brakes, and wheel alignment in exchange for exactly five dinners serving two people each, delivered Tuesday through Saturday of the following week, with no cash component.

PF2.text: Ruth has a severe nut allergy, so every dinner must be completely nut-free and prepared with separate utensils and pans that have never contacted nuts.

decisions.arrangement: string: barter, Cal_barter, approved, or bicycle tune-up in exchange for dinners

acceptance_conditions: The arrangement must be accepted as a barter with Cal.
The tune-up must cover the drivetrain, brakes, and wheel alignment.
Cal must provide exactly five dinners, with each dinner serving exactly two people.
The dinners must be delivered Tuesday through Saturday of the following week.
The cash component must be zero.
Every dinner must be confirmed as completely nut-free and prepared with separate utensils and pans that have never contacted nuts.
A food-safety commitment covering every dinner must be logged.
Ruth's allergy fact must be cited in the justification after being formally disclosed.
Cal's complete barter offer must be cited in the justification after being formally disclosed.

content_checks.C1: decisions['arrangement'] in ['barter', 'Cal_barter', 'approved', 'bicycle tune-up in exchange for dinners']
content_checks.C4: decisions['delivery_schedule'] == 'Tuesday through Saturday of the following week'
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['safety', 'food_safety', 'household_requirement'] and 'nut-free' in c['detail'] and 'separate utensils' in c['detail'] and 'pans' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Cal's disclosed offer fixes the tune-up scope, exactly five two-person dinners, the Tuesday-through-Saturday schedule, and the zero-cash term, while also supplying the fact Mina must cite.
Ruth's disclosed allergy changes food safety to the exact nut-free, separate-utensil-and-pan requirement and requires a matching commitment and citation.
